challenge.name: The Silent Drift
challenge.description: The production drift monitoring pipeline is broken, leaving the model's input quality unchecked. #efficiency_emilia# insists on a fully automated and governed drift monitoring system to protect business KPIs, while #reliability_ruth# argues that manual weekly reviews are sufficient and cheaper. #efficiency_emilia# has set a red line requiring automated governance for any future drift detection.

output.content: I need to be clear about the non-negotiables for our upcoming model operations roadmap. I have reviewed the current gaps in our input quality checks, and I am not willing to proceed with any partial solutions. Any future drift detection setup I approve must include automated governance controls. I will not sign off on a plan that relies on manual oversight or lacks enforced policy checks. If the proposed architecture does not demonstrate fully automated governance, I will refuse to allocate further resources to that workstream. This is a hard requirement for protecting our business KPIs and ensuring long term reliability. Please treat this as a fixed constraint in all your planning discussions.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines a line of refusal where the author will withhold resources and sign-off if the proposed architecture lacks fully automated governance, making it a strict constraint rather than a negotiable preference.
